To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number of intensity resolution steps is not a major limiting factor in consonant recognition, but that it is a limiting factor in sentence recognition.
the performance of the cochlear implant subject is limited by the number of channels, not the number of intensity levels.

(a) the number of channels is more important than the number of intensity resolution steps in determining speech perception; and (b) the number of intensity levels needed to reach asymptotically high levels of speech recognition is a function of the speech material, and the number of frequency bands processed by the device.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the physical properties of the acoustic signal and the psychophysical and perceptual properties of the signal.
how to optimize speech perception by cochlear implant subjects.
the role of spectral and intensity resolution in determining the speech recognition abilities of cochlear implant users.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the performance of normal-hearing listeners is primarily limited by spectral resolution, whereas the performance of cochleae implant listeners is primarily limited, in terms of speech understanding, by the number of channels received.
speech recognition by cochlear implant listeners is primarily a function of spectral resolution.
the performance of CI listeners is not affected by the reduced dynamic range of the CI processor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
spectral resolution is the primary limiting factor in speech recognition for cochlear implant listeners and intensity resolution is a minor factor.
the performance of CI users can be improved by increasing the number of channels, but not by increasing the number or intensity steps.

the number of intensity levels needed for asymptotic consonant recognition performance by normal-hearing subjects and cochlear implant users is a function of the speech material used and the spectral resolution available.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when spectral resolution is poor, the number of intensity resolution steps needs to be increased to achieve high levels.
the performance of normal-hearing listeners is not affected by the number of steps used to quantize speech, as long as the number of steps is greater than or equal to the number of channels used.
speech recognition is primarily limited by spectral resolution, and that intensity resolution can be traded off for spectral resolution.
